message.content: {"key_mechanism_gt": "The incorporation of a carefully selected modulator during the synthesis of covalent-organic frameworks will slow monomer incorporation kinetics, leading to the formation of highly ordered crystalline structures with amplified surface area, larger crystal domains, refined pore distribution, and enhanced stability, collectively resulting in superior Modulator-Assisted COFs (MA-COFs).", "key_mechanism_gen": "The modulator temporarily occupies active linker sites to reduce instantaneous monomer reactivity, thereby extending the kinetic window for thermodynamic equilibration and error correction of non-covalent interactions prior to irreversible covalent bond formation.", "recovery": "RECOVERED", "rationale": "Both hypotheses describe the same core mechanism of modulator-mediated kinetic control to improve crystallinity and stability, with the generated hypothesis providing a more detailed mechanistic explanation of site occupation and error correction."}
